steps.t: A Socket at the branch bonds any available last miles into active/active tunnels to the nearest PoP.
The PoP applies app- and identity-aware QoS, TCP acceleration and packet-loss mitigation in the path.
Traffic crosses the global private backbone, Tier-1 carrier diverse, with a 99.999 % SLA between PoPs.
The datacentre socket and the AWS vSocket are reached privately; the single MPLS circuit is retired.

Two fpins on the ring: 'Manchester PoP' (left, halo, f-s under it 'nearest PoP — selected automatically') and 'London PoP' (right). Both branch tunnels terminate on the Manchester pin. network-sdwan.title: Glasgow branch on-net over dual last miles and the Cato global private backbone
network-sdwan.desc: A Glasgow branch joins the WAN over broadband and 4G/LTE active/active tunnels to its nearest PoP, crosses the SLA-backed global private backbone, and reaches the London DC socket and the AWS vSocket; the single MPLS circuit it replaces is retired.
carry: Socket X1600 at the Glasgow branch; Socket X1500 at London DC; vSocket in AWS eu-west-2
Two last miles named: broadband and 4G/LTE, both active/active
Manchester PoP labelled as the nearest PoP, selected automatically; London PoP as the far end
99.999 % uptime SLA between PoPs; Tier-1 carrier diversity; TCP acceleration; packet-loss mitigation
Legacy MPLS: 'One circuit · no on-ramp', marked retired at cutover with a red cross

steps.t: Acquired sites are defined as code and created through the Cato GraphQL API with Terraform.
Zero-touch Sockets ship to each acquired site and connect to the nearest PoP as they are plugged in.
The acquired estate joins the global backbone and reaches London DC under the existing converged policy.
Entra ID provisions acquired users and groups, so WAN firewall rules can name them from day one.

network-agility-mna.title: M&A onboarding: acquired sites deployed through the Cato API onto the global backbone
network-agility-mna.desc: Terraform pushes acquired-site definitions through the Cato API, zero-touch Sockets connect each site to the nearest PoP, Entra ID provisions the acquired users and groups, and the acquired estate reaches London DC and the HQ lab site over the global private backbone.
legend: Acquired-site traffic — on-net over the backbone
Control plane — API site creation · Entra ID provisioning

Microsoft Entra ID — acquired-company tenant; 'SCIM — users & groups provisioned' as a dashed control-plane line
Terraform · Cato API — 'Site definitions as code' and 'Sites created via GraphQL API'

Existing estate: London DC (Socket X1500 · core apps) and On-prem lab (Socket X1500 · HQ)

steps.t: The datacentre takes a Socket first and becomes the bridge between the Cato cloud and the MPLS network.
The DC socket advertises the prefixes of sites still on MPLS, reached via the DC LAN and the MPLS CE router.
Each branch migrates on its own schedule with broadband and 4G last miles, reaching the DC over the backbone.
Migrated sites reach un-migrated sites by transiting the DC; the legacy network is untouched until switch-off.

diagram.brief: 760x560, three columns. A fl-tun from the Cato cloud down into the DC Socket. RIGHT: cloud(…, 'MPLS', 'legacy — unchanged', cls default) in grey/net styling, then site(…,'LEEDS — ON MPLS') with nd 'Leeds' / subs '192.168.3.0/24 · CE router' and 'migrates at contract end' (icon building, cls soft). fl-net (np:0) from the DC MPLS CE router to the MPLS cloud and on to Leeds. FLOWS: (1) Bristol ↔ London DC: fl-tun up to the Cato cloud and fl-tun down to the DC Socket, particles both ways (label 'Bristol ↔ London DC — on-net via Cato'). Narrative: new WAN on the left, bridge in the middle, old WAN on the right, with the transit path drawn through the bridge.

network-mpls-migration.title: MPLS co-existence during migration: Bristol on Cato, Leeds on MPLS, London DC bridging both
network-mpls-migration.desc: Bristol, already migrated to a Socket with broadband and 4G last miles, reaches London DC over the Cato cloud and reaches Leeds, still on MPLS, by transiting the DC socket, local firewall and MPLS CE router; nothing on the legacy network changes until Leeds migrates.
legend: Bristol ↔ London DC — on-net via Cato
Bristol ↔ Leeds — transits London DC during co-existence
Legacy MPLS — unchanged until Leeds migrates

London DC: Socket X1500 (demo tenant runs an X1500, not the deck's X1700) advertising Leeds' prefix; local firewall for internet egress today; MPLS CE router routing 192.168.3.0/24
Leeds: on MPLS, CE router, migrates at contract end
Pill 'One routing table for all sites' on the Cato cloud

steps.t: A branch user's traffic to a cloud workload enters the nearest PoP and crosses the private backbone.
The cloud DC attaches by vSocket HA pair, IPsec from a native gateway, or a layer-2 cross-connect at the PoP.
The WAN firewall governs branch-to-VPC traffic with the same rulebase and audit trail as physical sites.
Egress to the VPC happens at the PoP nearest the cloud region, never across the public internet middle mile.

diagram.brief: 760x560, left-to-right. LEFT: two nd boxes — 'Glasgow' / sub 'Branch · Socket X1600' (icon building) and 'London DC' / sub 'Socket X1500 · datacentre' (icon server) — each joined by fl-tun to an fpin 'London PoP' on the left of a central ring() labelled 'Cato Global Private Backbone'. A fl-hot arc along the ring front from the London PoP to a second fpin 'Cloud-adjacent PoP' (halo) on the right. RIGHT: four cloud destination boxes stacked (R soft with small cloud() glyph), each joined from the cloud-adjacent pin by a differently-classed line: (1) 'Azure VNet · UK South' / sub 'Azure-UKS-Hub-vSocket' with a pill 'vSocket HA pair' and an 'HA' amber pill — line fl-tun labelled 'vSocket · DTLS'; (2) 'AWS VPC · eu-west-2' / sub 'AWS eu-west-2' with pill 'vSocket HA pair' + 'HA' — line fl-tun labelled 'vSocket · DTLS'; (3) 'Azure Virtual WAN' / sub 'Azure vWAN hub' — line fl-ipsec labelled 'IPsec · IKEv2', note f-s 'IPsec from the vWAN hub'; (4) 'AWS region' / sub 'Cloud Interconnect' — line fl-priv (np:0 or slow) labelled 'L2 cross-connect', note f-s 'Cloud interconnect at the PoP'. Narrative: physical estate on the left, one backbone in the middle, three attachment methods fanning out to four cloud destinations on the right.

network-cloud-datacenter.title: Cloud datacentres connected to the Cato WAN by vSocket, IPsec and cross-connect
network-cloud-datacenter.desc: Glasgow and London DC reach every cloud datacentre across the global private backbone: an Azure VNet and an AWS VPC attach by vSocket HA pairs, Azure Virtual WAN by IPsec, and an AWS region by a layer-2 cross-connect at the PoP, all under the same policy and visibility.
legend: IPsec · IKEv2 from the cloud gateway
Layer-2 cross-connect at the PoP (no tunnel)
Backbone — same policy as physical sites
carry: Glasgow (Branch · Socket X1600) and London DC (Socket X1500 · datacentre) as the physical estate
Azure VNet · UK South — Azure-UKS-Hub-vSocket, vSocket HA pair; AWS VPC · eu-west-2 — vSocket HA pair (HA pills on both)
Azure Virtual WAN — Azure vWAN hub, IPsec · IKEv2 from the vWAN hub
AWS region — Cloud Interconnect, L2 cross-connect at the PoP
London PoP and a 'Cloud-adjacent PoP' on the backbone; egress at the PoP nearest the cloud region

steps.t: The Sydney site enters its nearest PoP, where voice, video and bulk traffic are classified and prioritised.
Traffic rides the private backbone with TCP acceleration and packet-loss mitigation applied between PoPs.
Latency to the London DC is consistent, hop by hop, instead of varying with public-internet peering.
Microsoft 365 leaves the backbone at the PoP nearest the application instance, not at a UK breakout.

TOP BAND (Cato): tier label 'Cato Global Private Backbone' with f-s 'Tier-1 carrier diversity · optimal routing per packet · 99.999 % SLA between PoPs'. LEFT: nd 'aws-sydney-ipsec' / sub 'Sydney · IPsec site' (icon cloud/cpu) joined by fl-ipsec to fpin 'Sydney PoP' (halo) with f-s 'nearest PoP — QoS applied at ingress'; beside the pin a vertical chip stack of three pills: 'voice P1' (g), 'video P2' (g), 'bulk P3' (m) — the QoS queues. RIGHT: fpin 'London PoP' feeding two destinations by fl-tun / fl-flow: nd 'London DC' / sub 'Socket X1500 · file servers' (icon server) and cloud() 'Microsoft 365' / sub 'egress near the app' reached by a fl-flow with arrow (smart egress). BOTTOM BAND (contrast): a long fl-net grey path (np:0) from Sydney to London with five hop dots like the backbone figure's public-internet path and a pill 'Public internet — variable latency, jitter and loss · no SLA'. No blocking marks; the contrast path is grey, not red. Node count 9 (Sydney site, Sydney PoP, 3 mid PoPs, London PoP, London DC, M365, QoS stack). Narrative: left to right, Sydney in, QoS at ingress, consistent backbone, London DC and M365 out; the internet alternative runs beneath.

network-global-app-performance.title: Sydney to London application traffic over the Cato global private backbone
network-global-app-performance.desc: A Sydney IPsec site enters the Sydney PoP, where QoS prioritises voice, video and bulk traffic, crosses a chain of backbone PoPs with consistent latency to the London PoP, and reaches the London DC socket and Microsoft 365 via smart egress; the public internet path beneath shows variable latency and no SLA.
legend: Sydney IPsec site to its nearest PoP
carry: aws-sydney-ipsec — Sydney · IPsec site (the demo-tenant site the runbook uses)
QoS queues at ingress: voice P1, video P2, bulk P3
Label 'SYD → LDN ~280 ms — consistent, every packet (illustrative)' — keep the word illustrative
London DC — Socket X1500 · file servers; Microsoft 365 — egress near the app
99.999 % SLA between PoPs; Tier-1 carrier diversity; optimal routing per packet
Public internet contrast: variable latency, jitter and loss · no SLA

steps.t: Azure, AWS and GCP can attach by vSocket — a Cato VM in the VNet or VPC building DTLS tunnels to the PoP.
All four clouds, including OCI, can attach by IPsec from the provider's native VPN gateway.
A private layer-2 Cloud Interconnect circuit via a fabric provider reaches the PoP with no tunnel.
Whichever door is used, the tenant lands on the same backbone, policy set and console as every site.

diagram.brief: 760x560, three columns left-to-right. LEFT column: four cloud tiles (R soft + small cloud glyph): 'Azure' / sub 'VNets · vWAN'; 'AWS' / sub 'VPCs · TGW'; 'GCP' / sub 'VPCs · Cloud Router'; 'OCI' / sub 'VCNs · DRG' with a red-class pill 'no vSocket option' under it. MIDDLE column: three on-ramp nd boxes (cls hot): 'vSocket' / subs 'Azure · AWS · GCP' and 'Cato VM in the VNet/VPC' (icon cpu); 'IPsec site' / subs 'all four clouds' and 'native VPN gateway · IKEv2' (icon lock); 'Cloud Interconnect' / subs 'all four clouds' and 'private L2 via fabric' (icon plug). RIGHT: all three doors converge by their own line class (fl-tun, fl-ipsec, fl-priv) on one fpin 'Cato PoP' (halo) sitting on a ring() labelled 'Cato Global Private Backbone'; pill (cls g) under the pin 'one policy set · one console'. No branch/DC nodes needed (the backbone ring implies the rest of the estate). Node count 8 (4 clouds, 3 doors, 1 PoP pin) plus ring. Narrative: four clouds, three doors, one WAN; OCI is the one cloud with two doors only.

network-cloud-connectivity.title: Azure, AWS, GCP and OCI reaching the Cato backbone via vSocket, IPsec or Cloud Interconnect
network-cloud-connectivity.desc: Four clouds on the left reach one Cato PoP through three doors — vSocket for Azure, AWS and GCP, IPsec from any native gateway, and a private layer-2 Cloud Interconnect circuit — and every door lands on the same backbone, policy set and console; OCI has no vSocket option.
legend: Cloud Interconnect — private L2 circuit, no tunnel, no encryption overhead
carry: Four clouds with their constructs: Azure (VNets · vWAN), AWS (VPCs · TGW), GCP (VPCs · Cloud Router), OCI (VCNs · DRG)
OCI marked 'no vSocket option'; OCI's doors are IPsec or FastConnect into Cloud Interconnect
vSocket: Azure · AWS · GCP, 'Cato VM in the VNet/VPC'; IPsec site: all four clouds, 'native VPN gateway · IKEv2'; Cloud Interconnect: all four clouds, 'private L2 via fabric'
Cato PoP on the Cato Global Private Backbone — 'one policy set · one console'
The interconnect circuit is private but unencrypted (no encryption overhead) — the legend wording must not call it encrypted

steps.t: Public clouds land their private-link services on an exchange fabric such as Equinix Fabric or Megaport.
A private datacentre or colo cage reaches the same fabric by physical cross-connect — no socket, no tunnel.
One VLAN-coordinated layer-2 circuit carries both into the Cato PoP, where the security stack already sits.
The interconnect site is just a site: same policy, visibility and backbone routing to branches and users.

From the fabric one thick fl-priv line labelled pill 'dedicated layer-2 · private, deterministic' into an fpin 'Cato PoP' (halo) with f-s under it 'VLAN handoff · FWaaS · IPS'. RIGHT: nd 'Branch site' / sub 'Bristol Office · Socket' (icon building) joined to the ring by fl-tun, and nd 'Remote users' / sub 'SDP Client · ZTNA' (icon users) joined by fl-https. A fl-hot arc on the ring front from the PoP to the right-hand side. CONTRAST LANE above: a fl-ha (amber) dashed path from the Public clouds box arching over the fabric straight to the PoP through a small cloud() labelled 'Public internet' / sub 'best-effort · variable', pill (cls y) 'Traditional IPsec over the internet — the path this replaces'. Nothing red; the old path is amber, not failed. Node count 8 (public clouds, private DC, fabric, PoP pin, internet cloud, branch, users) plus ring. Narrative: two kinds of peer converge on one fabric, one wire into the PoP, the whole WAN on the far side; the amber lane shows what the wire replaces.

network-cloud-interconnect.title: Cloud Interconnect: public clouds and a private datacentre reach the Cato PoP over one layer-2 circuit
network-cloud-interconnect.desc: Public clouds via their private-link services and a private datacentre via physical cross-connect converge on an exchange fabric such as Equinix Fabric or Megaport; one VLAN-coordinated layer-2 circuit carries both into the Cato PoP and onto the global private backbone, replacing IPsec over the public internet.
legend: Traditional IPsec over the internet — the path this replaces
carry: Public clouds: AWS · Azure · GCP · OCI via private-link services (ExpressRoute / Direct Connect / Partner Interconnect / FastConnect class)
Private datacentre: Customer DC · colo cage via physical cross-connect
Exchange fabric: Equinix Fabric · Megaport — 'one VLAN, all parties'
Cato PoP: 'VLAN handoff · FWaaS · IPS'; branch archetype 'Bristol Office · Socket'; remote users 'SDP Client · ZTNA'
No socket appliance and no IPsec tunnel anywhere in the interconnect data path; the circuit is private but unencrypted (MD5 is BGP auth only)
Redundancy is active/passive to two PoPs — do not imply load-sharing if a second PoP is drawn

steps.t: A branch LAN behind a Cisco ASA joins Cato over IPsec — a route-based VTI on IKEv2, or a crypto map on IKEv1.
The primary tunnel lands on an allocated IP at the nearest PoP; the secondary on one at an alternate PoP.
If every primary tunnel drops, routes fail over to the secondary — IPsec sites never roam PoPs on their own.
From the PoP, traffic rides the backbone to Socket sites, cloud datacentres and secure internet egress.

LEFT inside site(…,'BRANCH BEHIND CISCO ASA'): nd 'Branch LAN' / sub '10.20.0.0/24' (icon laptop/users) joined by fl-lan to nd (cls hot) 'Cisco ASA' / subs '203.0.113.10 · outside' and 'VTI (IKEv2) / crypto map (IKEv1)' (icon firewall). Narrative: an existing ASA on the left, two tunnels to two fixed allocated IPs at two PoPs, the full WAN and secure egress on the right.

network-ipsec-asa.title: Cisco ASA site connected to Cato over dual IPsec tunnels
network-ipsec-asa.desc: A branch LAN behind a Cisco ASA runs a primary IPsec tunnel to a Cato allocated IP at the nearest PoP and a standby secondary tunnel to an allocated IP at an alternate PoP; both PoPs join the global private backbone, which carries traffic to the London DC socket, an AWS vSocket and secure internet egress.
legend: Backbone to Socket and vSocket sites
carry: Branch LAN 10.20.0.0/24; Cisco ASA outside 203.0.113.10 (documentation-range placeholders)
Primary — London PoP, Allocated IP 198.51.100.10; Secondary — Manchester, Allocated IP 198.51.100.20
'VTI (IKEv2) / crypto map (IKEv1)' on the ASA node
Destinations: London DC (Socket X1500 · apps), AWS eu-west-2 (vSocket HA pair), SaaS & internet (Secure egress at PoP)
Secondary tunnel is standby, not load-sharing; IPsec sites do not roam PoPs automatically

steps.t: The backbone of 100+ PoPs already exists in the target region, with the full security stack in every PoP.
A zero-touch Socket ships direct to the new office; anyone who can plug in power and WAN installs it.
The landing team works from day one on the Cato Client or over IPsec while the hardware is in transit.
The new site inherits the same policy and visibility as London DC the moment it connects to its nearest PoP.

Narrative: existing estate on the left, new regions landing on their nearest PoP across the ring, China joining compliantly through a licensed partner in the corner.

network-global-expansion.title: A growing global footprint joining the Cato backbone through nearest PoPs
network-global-expansion.desc: The existing London DC connects to the London PoP; new sites join on their nearest PoPs — Madrid over a zero-touch Socket, Sydney over IPsec, and a new plant whose day-one users are on the Cato Client while its Socket is in transit — and a Shanghai office joins compliantly through a licensed local partner.
legend: IPsec on day one, no Cato hardware
Users on the Cato Client while hardware ships
Compliant China on-ramp via licensed local partner

Madrid Office — Socket X1600 · zero-touch; aws-sydney-ipsec — Sydney · IPsec · day one
New plant — Day 1: 'Users on Cato Client' and 'Socket X1500 in transit'

Shanghai office — 'Compliant on-ramp', 'via licensed partner', 'in-country presence', 'licensed local partner' — nothing more specific about China (no cities, licensing detail or in-country routing claims)

steps.t: Every link is scored every second on loss, jitter and latency; a cut last mile re-homes flows to the survivor.
On critical sites an HA Socket pair takes over after 3 s of missed keepalives; LTE idles as the last resort.
If every link fails the SLA against the current PoP, the Socket moves to another — preferred PoPs steer it.
With no PoP reachable, Internet and WAN Recovery keep traffic moving off-cloud, uninspected but working.

diagram.brief: 760x560, bottom-to-top inside one site frame, Cato at the top like the branch figure. TOP: ring() 'Global Private Backbone' with two fpins: 'PoP 1 — London' (left, f-s 'primary preferred') and 'PoP 2 — Manchester' (right, f-s 'secondary preferred'). network-resilient-site-design.title: Critical site resilience: HA Socket pair, diverse last miles, LTE last resort and two PoPs
network-resilient-site-design.desc: A critical site runs an HA pair of X1700 Sockets with VRRP keepalives, two diverse last miles and an LTE last-resort link; the primary last mile to PoP 1 has failed and every flow has re-homed over the second last mile to PoP 2, while the standby Socket and the idle LTE link stay in reserve on the Cato global private backbone.
legend: Active last mile — carries all flows
LTE last resort — idle, minimal system traffic
Failed last mile — flows re-homed by SLA scoring
carry: Socket A — X1700, HA master · active; Socket B — X1700, Standby · Ready; VRRP keepalive, 3 s → failover
LTE / 5G modem — precedence 3 · last resort, 'idle until wired links fail' (carries only minimal system traffic while idle)
PoP 1 — London (primary preferred); PoP 2 — Manchester (secondary preferred)
ISP A fibre — cut (red X); ISP B — all flows re-home
Site LAN — users · servers · OT
Do not draw LTE as carrying traffic (off-cloud transport is disabled on precedence-3 links and it is idle in this scene)
